summary: Adds a short-lived platform identity contract for authorized tenant lifecycle control-plane calls and closes direct shard mutations in managed mode.
userImpact: Authorized platform operators can exchange their current host session for a short-lived identity limited to tenant read or tenant management operations.
Self-hosted deployments keep the existing direct tenant lifecycle routes unless cloud-required mode is enabled.

instructions: Managed pooled shards configure a distinct platform Cloud identity audience before enabling cloud-required mode.
Control-plane consumers must verify the exact issuer, audience, key ID, platform action, shard ID, lifetime, and signature before accepting an assertion.

configuration: Adds EG_PLATFORM_CLOUD_IDENTITY_AUDIENCE for a distinct platform control-plane audience; cloud-required startup fails when it is absent.
EG_TENANCY_CLOUD_REQUIRED=true rejects direct POST and PATCH /api/platform/tenants mutations while retaining authenticated tenant reads and workload lifecycle routes.

changes: Adds POST /api/platform/cloud-identity with a strict platform.tenants.read or platform.tenants.manage request action and a short-lived ES256 response.
Direct platform tenant mutations return 503 in cloud-required mode so managed control-plane orchestration cannot be bypassed through a shard-local browser session.

notes: No schema change is required; identity issuance is stateless and the existing TypeORM tenant lifecycle remains authoritative outside cloud-required direct-user mutation paths.

security: The host authenticates the current user and evaluates the exact requested platform.tenants.read or platform.tenants.manage authorization action before signing.
Assertions expire after 90 seconds, use a platform-specific audience and schema, and contain no tenant record, SSO configuration, provider assertion, secret, or browser credential.
Cloud-required mode fails closed before invoking direct shard-local tenant create or update services.
documentation: Documents the platform Cloud identity claims, authorization boundary, managed-mode mutation fence, verifier requirements, configuration, rollback, and cloud-neutral ownership boundary.
knownLimitations: OSS issues and documents the neutral assertion but does not implement a cloud control-plane endpoint or vendor-specific identity exchange.
rollback: Disable managed control-plane callers before removing the platform audience or rolling back the host.
Turn off cloud-required mode only when operators intentionally accept restored direct shard-local tenant mutation.
validation: Focused schema, signing, route authorization, OpenAPI, configuration, and fail-closed mutation tests cover the additive contract.
PostgreSQL remains the primary pooled-mode feedback lane; all supported database adapters require candidate portability qualification even though this change adds no migration.
